text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
Brazil's four leading carmakers, Volkswagen, Fiat, Gerneral Motors and Ford, will together channel $5.7 billion into the market to promote car sales in an increasingly competitive environment.
-- TELEBRAS TO BE DIVIDED INTO FOUR BLOCKS

Telecommunications Minister Sergio Motta said Brazil's state telecommunications firm Telebras will be privatized in four blocks with Sao Paulo's Telesp going to auction this year and the other three blocks in 1998.

The government omitted by mistake imports worth $650 million by state oil giant Petrobras in January's trade balance calculations which led to an incorrect trade surplus of $60 million. Publication of the trade figures has been postponed until Friday.
-- CARDOSO WANTS STABLE FUNDING FOR HEALTH

Cardoso said the government would have to find sources for stable funding of the health system this year since the new so-called CPMF cheque tax, which is funding health provisions this year, is only temporary.
-- CVRD'S UNEXPLORED DEPOSITS EXCLUDED FROM AUCTION

The government has decided to exclude from the privatization of mining giant CVRD those mineral deposits in northern Brazil which have not yet been evaluated, but are believed to contain large amounts of gold and copper.
-- TEMER AND MAGALHAES GUARANTEE MAJORITY FOR CARDOSO

With the election of Michel Temer as new president of the Chamber of Deputies the government of Fernando Henrique has scored a further victory following the election of another government ally, Antonio Carlos Magalhaes, as Senate president.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
